newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on central bank comments.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on central bank comments.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended lower on Tuesday after rebounding sharply from an intra-day nadir.
The weighted index plunged at the opening but ended only 45.15 points or 0.59 percent lower at 7,642.03.
Turnover was a hectic T$139 billion.
The market's late rally came despite bearish comments by central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong that the index had risen too much recently, brokers said.
The market also was hit by rumours that China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health had deteriorated, prompting Beijing leaders to cancel official trips.
The index had plunged 162.47 points at the opening after Sheu said early on Tuesday that Taiwan's stock market had "risen slightly too much recently."
"Sheu's comments made many investors worry that the government may launch measures to try and slow down the market's growth," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
Before Tuesday the market had finished higher in 10 of its last 11 sessions and gained more than 500 points during that span.
Despite the market's poor start on Tuesday, momentum returned by mid-session as many bargain hunters decided to enter the market following its initial drop.

"The fact that the market recovered quickly after such a bad start on Tuesday meant investors were still very confident about the market's outlook, and they were just looking for an opportunity to buy," Fang said.
The heavily weighted financials fell by 1.63 percent, with recently hot China Development Corp losing T$3.50 or 3.26 percent to T$104.
But electronics shares supported the market by rising 0.51 percent.
Blue-chip Acer Inc gained T$3, or 5.13 percent, to T$61.50.
Brokers expected the market to remain in a consolidation on Wednesday with a range of 7,580-7,680.
